conventions.convention: Curves are continuous and locally absolutely continuous in smooth charts. Future causal velocity must exist, be nonzero and be future causal almost everywhere; constant curves are excluded from this class. Causal reachability separately includes p=q.
Future and past inextendibility mean absence of a point limit in the specified ambient manifold at the upper and lower parameter ends, including infinite ends. Causal past is inverse reachability.
Global hyperbolicity means strong causality plus compact causal diamonds. A temporal function has past-directed timelike gradient, so its differential is positive on future causal vectors.

A Cauchy set has exactly one parameter visit on every inextendible causal curve, rather than merely one distinct image point. Achronality and acausality here exclude relations between distinct points only; this differs on chronology-violating models from Minguzzi's Definitions 2.19 and 2.95.

The future hypersurface normal satisfies g(n,n)=-1. The second fundamental form is K(V,W)=g(∇_V n,W), and matter projections are ρ=T(n,n), j(V)=-T(n,V). Thus the constraint projections are G(n,n)-Λ=κρ and G(n,V)=-κj(V).

Congruences are smooth future unit timelike fields with ∇_n n=0. B_ab=∇_b n_a, θ=g^{ab}B_ab, shear subtracts θh/3, and vorticity is B's antisymmetric part. Their affine flow parameter s gives metric proper time s/c.
The flat model is R⁴ with η=diag(-1,1,1,1) and N=∂₀. Its future closed coordinate cone is v⁰≥|v_s| and includes zero; future causal vectors exclude zero.

Countable Choice and Dependent Choice are explicit premises of the general absolutely continuous calculus and its consuming flat-model results. In the maximal-geodesic lemma, the additional endpoint-integration assumptions are scoped to clause (a).

load_bearing.statement: Under Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, local absolute continuity is chart-independent and admits finite compact-interval subdivisions; velocity and smooth composition obey the chain rule almost everywhere; piecewise C¹ curves, finite concatenations and increasing C¹ diffeomorphic reparametrizations have the stated causal properties; causal reachability is reflexive and transitive, and chronological reachability implies causal reachability.

A Cauchy set S has exactly one element in γ⁻¹[S] for every inextendible causal curve γ. A Cauchy hypersurface is also a spacelike embedded hypersurface. D⁺(S) tests all past-inextendible causal curves through the point, and D⁻(S) tests all future-inextendible ones.

Under the clause-(a) choice premises, a future causal curve converging at a finite upper parameter endpoint has a parameter-preserving causal extension. Every maximal geodesic with nonzero initial velocity has no point limit at either finite or infinite end. Every compact causal segment lies on an inextendible causal curve, up to increasing affine identification, and every Cauchy set is acausal.

A spacelike embedded hypersurface has a unique future unit normal, smooth along the hypersurface with extension-independent tangential derivative. Its induced metric is Riemannian, K(V,W)=g(∇_V n,W) is smooth and symmetric, and ∇_V n is its self-adjoint shape operator applied to V.

Under Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, inertial time is strictly increasing along future causal curves in the flat model; spatial increments are bounded by time increments. Future/past inextendible ends have time supremum +∞/infimum -∞, and x⁰ is temporal with gradient -∂₀.

Under Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, J⁺(p)=p+the future closed cone and I⁺(p)=p+the future open cone. Every inertial time level is a Cauchy hypersurface; causal diamonds are compact; the flat model is strongly causal and globally hyperbolic.
For smooth fields V,Z, Vᶜ∇_c(∇_aZᵃ)=∇_a(Vᶜ∇_cZᵃ)−(∇_aVᶜ)(∇_cZᵃ)−Ric_cd VᶜZᵈ, with curvature and Ricci conventions fixed by the cited curvature definition.

Along a smooth future unit timelike geodesic congruence, θ′=−θ²/3−σ_abσ^{ab}+ω_abω^{ab}−Ric(n,n). If ω=0, Ric(n,n)≥0 and θ₀<0, then θ remains negative and 1/(−θ(s))≤1/(−θ₀)−(s−s₀)/3; the maximal flow interval in the congruence region has supremum at most s₀+3/(−θ₀). Only continuations preserving the stated hypotheses are excluded.

concerns.concern: Definition (e) gives H⁺(S)=D⁺(S) minus I⁻(D⁺(S)), but describes this as points 'not chronologically preceded by any point of D⁺(S)'. Membership in I⁻(D⁺(S)) means preceding some point of D⁺(S), not being preceded. The displayed formula agrees with Minguzzi Definition 3.14, printed p. 87; the verbal description reverses its direction.

Definition (d), after the universal embedding condition, says 'Thus maximality is uniqueness up to data-fixing isometry among globally hyperbolic developments with their selected stress-energy tensors.' Universal absorption does not say that all globally hyperbolic developments are isometric. For flat data at t=1/2 with T=0, Minkowski space and its open slab (0,1)×R³ are both developments under (c), but one is geodesically complete and the other is incomplete. The displayed universal property should not be equated with uniqueness among arbitrary developments.

Definition (c) calls a development globally hyperbolic when its embedded initial surface is Cauchy, 'so that' the spacetime is globally hyperbolic. The earlier definition requires strong causality and compact diamonds; the cited batch-75 definitions do not prove Cauchy implies those conditions. The page and scope remark explicitly defer that substantial implication, which is supplied later by thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic. The current definition silently uses the deferred theorem rather than requiring both properties or marking this implication as deferred.

The first Remark explains the inertial slices as Cauchy 'because they are entire level sets of a temporal function'. Entire temporal levels alone do not suffice. In Minkowski space u=t−sqrt(1+(x¹)²) is temporal, but its nonempty entire level u=1 is missed by the inextendible null line γ(s)=(s,s,0,0). The correct additional input for the example's inertial time is its full range on every inextendible causal curve, supplied by lem-gr-flat-time-monotonicity-and-lipschitz-graphs (c).

The item is domain mathematics and declares the SI and ideal-clock suppliers only through motivated_by, yet Example (ii) and Verification 2.1 include the conditional ideal-clock identification and say 'This proves (ii)'. The length and metric proper-time calculation is mathematical; the clock-reading identification uses a physical postulate. Its placement inside the proved claim and verification blurs the declared nonlogical role. The physical qualifications are explicit and no measurement is fabricated, but the contextual interpretation should be clearly separated from the mathematical verification.

alerts.finding: Fact [L1] restates the future causal criterion as 'v⁰≥|v_vec|>0', citing lem-gr-flat-inertial-cone-criterion-and-sums. The supplier requires v≠0 and v⁰≥|v_vec|, which implies v⁰>0 but does not imply |v_vec|>0. The vector (2,0,0,0), which is this example's total displacement r−p, is future timelike and causal but fails the stated criterion.

The comparison Remark says coordinate time t has 'gradient field ... ∂₀'. With the declared metric diag(-1,1,1,1), ∇t=−∂₀. The normalized future field ∇t/g(∇t,∇t) is ∂₀. Proof 1.1 already distinguishes these objects correctly for T; the comparison confuses them.

Definition (c) attributes 'openness of I± and the transitivity of' chronology to lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus clauses (d) and (f). Those clauses supply concatenation and reachability properties, not openness of chronology. The later well-definedness paragraph correctly cites lem-gr-chronology-openness and lem-gr-push-up-rule, so the missing support is available but the initial citation is overstrong.

The Statement introduces 'the Lorentzian length functional on future causal curves' by citing def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time. That supplier explicitly restricts length to piecewise-C¹ future timelike worldlines and denies a null extension. The broader Lebesgue length definition actually appears in lem-gr-normal-neighborhood-length-monotonicity, which is already a declared dependency. The Statement's defining citation should identify that broader supplier.

seams_checked.note: The scope remark treats the Einstein equation as an adopted physical law. The constraint lemma separately assumes the tensor equation mathematically and evaluates its normal projections; it does not claim empirical verification or existence of solutions.
Smooth boundaryless Lorentzian four-manifolds, signature, future pairing with N, inverse metric and metric-selected connection agree with the opened definitions.
Uses preserve nondegenerate Levi–Civita hypotheses, affine geodesic convention, nonzero-velocity qualifications, maximal domains and the restricted point-normal/radial-chart conclusions.
Observer normalization, positive-definite three-dimensional rest space, spatial projection and negative pairing with nonzero future causal vectors are used at their stated scope.
The commutator proof preserves R(∂c,∂d)∂b component order and Ric_bd=Rᵃ_bad. The resulting Raychaudhuri Ricci sign matches the supplier convention.

The slab's metric length and proper-time factor 1/c agree with the worldline definition. Its ideal-clock reading is expressly conditional, although its placement in the mathematical verification is recorded as a concern.
Flat signature, time orientation, causal classification and conditional SI length-coordinate interpretation are preserved; no numerical measurement is asserted.
The radial field is explicitly smooth, future unit timelike and geodesic on its open cone region, with the same observer/rest-space conventions.

Most inspected uses preserve continuity, AC_ω/DC, nonzero velocity, singleton Cauchy visits and no-limit inextendibility. However def-gr-future-and-past-sets (c) attributes chronology openness to causal-curve-calculus (d),(f), which do not state it; the separate openness supplier is cited later. Routed in alerts.

The slab and flat-model constructions retain the supplier hypotheses, but ex-gr-null-legs-corner-push-up [L1] strengthens the causal cone criterion incorrectly by requiring positive spatial norm. Routed in alerts.

Inspected uses preserve K=+g(∇n,·), normal projection signs, smooth normals and intrinsic ambient-region domains of dependence. The covector contracted commutator follows from the vector identity by metric compatibility. The later normal-frame theorem supplies Gauss–Codazzi rather than attributing it to the projection lemma.

Inspected causal and Cauchy uses preserve parameter visits, no-limit endpoints, ambient open-submanifold scope and maximal-geodesic qualifications. Its development definition explicitly adds fixed matter equations and complete matter data, and cites the later Cauchy-implies-global-hyperbolicity theorem; it does not infer these from the weaker batch-75 data definition.

The Minkowski example uses the actual flat Cauchy theorem and maximal-geodesic no-limit result. Surjectivity of the embedding is argued using complete source geodesics and target Cauchy crossings, rather than being inferred from existence of an embedding alone.
